Subject: Draft process: performance signal consensus & sensitive exception handling

Team —

Thanks for carving time this week. As we close Q2 reviews I want to surface a compact process for the cross-team stack comparisons and a safe path for handling a small set of sensitive rating exceptions (career-impacting). Goal: reach a consistent signal across leads while minimizing risk and preserving confidentiality.

Attached is a redacted workbook (2026-08-10_stack-comparisons-redacted.xlsx) with the stacks I pulled across Eng infra, Runtime, and Platform. Highlights:
- Three borderline cases where peer stacking diverges by more than one band.
- Two manager-initiated exception requests flagged for escalation (see notes column).

Proposed steps (short):
1) Quick sync between managers to agree on baseline signals for the contested stacks (up to 30m).
2) For any career-impacting exception: collect one-page rationale + evidence (metrics, goals ownership, 1-2 supporting peer statements) and share with People Ops counsel only.
3) If People Ops recommends moderation, we run a separate small panel (director + HR + one peer manager) and document rationale.
4) Finalize numbers in the HR system and notify folks with a calibrated messaging template.

Please review the workbook and add any missing context under the Notes tab. @Sarah — can you confirm whether the suggested evidence pack is sufficient from a compliance perspective (especially for performance-based reversals)?

I'd like to run the manager alignment call tomorrow 11:00–11:30 PT if that works. If not, propose alternate slots.

Thanks,
Markus

Hi all —

Thanks for the clear process. A few compliance / risk notes after a quick pass:
- Evidence pack: the items you listed are reasonable. Add: dated project deliverable link (or ticket id) and a single-line manager reflection about coaching history. That will make any audit trail defensible.
- Confidentiality: anonymize pre-reads (names -> codes) for any meeting that includes non-HR participants. Keep the sensitive PDFs in a restricted folder with access logs.
- Moderation panel: ensure at least one HR representative with decision authority is present (we can supply a contract HR lead if you need). Document dissenting opinions in the decision log.
- Notifications: timing matters. If a rating changes after the first manager conversation, the person should get a 1:1 before any formal notification.

I can join the call tomorrow if you want Sarah to be present live — I have 11:00–11:30 PT open.

Best,
